evidence.mission_note: A low-mile S52 manual M Roadster with a hardtop fits the future-keeper brief, but it is a keeper-only purchase priced above fair value. It conflicts with the current cash-preservation and bridge priorities unless the documentation proves it is a genuinely superior example.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes, by photo, a 5-speed Z3 M Roadster with 42,292 miles, a fitted hardtop, a clean-looking white body and two-tone interior, and no illuminated warning lamps with a mid-scale coolant gauge. Observed deviations from stock are an aftermarket twin-pipe exhaust replacing the quad tips and painted calipers. The seller also discloses two unspecified small imperfections and a radio needing programming. The car is photographed inside a collision repair centre, which is not evidence of damage but warrants a paint-meter check. No VIN, history report, title-brand statement or service record is provided. Both M-specific critical items, rear-subframe structure and cooling history, are therefore missing; S54 rod bearings do not apply to a 2000 S52 car. At $25,000 the ask exceeds the $18,439-$23,531 fair-value band, and comparable low-mileage roadsters have sold at $19.5-24k.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a title photo, any cooling-system receipts, and carpet-up trunk-floor plus underside subframe photos, and ask whether an independent BMW-specialist PPI can be arranged before any deposit.
